h1: S.D. Avenue Hotel Bangkok — a pool and spa hotel in Pinklao close to the Southern Bus Terminal
intro: Long-distance bus travellers heading south or west from Bangkok's Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai) often want more than just a room for the night — S.D. Avenue Hotel is a 3-star hotel on Borommaratchachonnani Road offering an outdoor pool, spa, massage, and a restaurant at an accessible price · it sits about 6 km from the terminal — a 15-minute Grab or taxi ride (no hotel shuttle) · the location is also convenient for Central Pinklao and local dining · prices start from about ฿1,300/night, with a score of 8.8 from 51 reviews on Trip.com

body.html: Who S.D. Avenue Hotel suits — to sum it up from real guest reviews in a single sentence: this hotel works best for travellers catching a long-distance bus south or west from Bangkok's Southern Bus Terminal who want a Thonburi-side stay with a pool, spa, and breakfast at under ฿2,000 a night · whether you are heading to Hua Hin, Phetchaburi, Kanchanaburi, Krabi, or Phuket — the Southern Bus Terminal is the departure point for all of those routes, and S.D. Avenue sits on the same Borommaratchachonnani Road · on the flip side, if you are hoping to walk to the terminal: be honest with yourself that no hotel in this area is walkable to Sai Tai Mai, because the terminal is tucked off the main road and sits in a non-residential zone — a Grab from this hotel takes about 15 minutes, which is the real logistics picture you need to set your expectations around.

Location and getting around — the hotel is at 94 Borommaratchachonnani Road, Bang Bumru, Bang Phlat, one of the main arteries of Bangkok's Thonburi west side that runs directly toward the Southern Bus Terminal · the distance from the hotel to the terminal is about 6 km — around 15 minutes by Grab or taxi · Grab fares in the early morning are typically ฿80–120 · the hotel has no shuttle, so plan to book a Grab in advance, especially for buses that depart at 4–6 a.m., when app-hailed cars can be harder to find · in the neighbourhood, the hotel is a short drive from Central Pinklao, walking distance from Lotus's Pinklao, and surrounded by local restaurants and markets · if you are driving yourself, the area connects conveniently to the expressway network and the hotel has on-site parking.
"Chose this place because it is in Pinklao — near Central Pinklao and a quick Grab ride to the Southern Bus Terminal. Room was spotless, staff were very helpful, great value for the price."

Room types and condition — S.D. Avenue has around 315 rooms across several categories · at the entry level, the Superior Room (No Window) starts at around ฿1,290/night — as the name says, no natural light, and best suited to someone who just needs a functional place to sleep before an early bus · stepping up, the Premier Room (floors 2 and 6, from ฿1,750) and the Deluxe Room (floors 11–12, from ฿2,100) give you windows and, on the higher floors, decent city views · the Deluxe Twin at 32 sqm fits two singles and a sofa bed, workable for three people · the Grand Deluxe Room (฿2,900 including breakfast) and the Junior Suite suit longer stays or guests who want more space · real guest reviews give the hotel a cleanliness score of 9.2, one of the highest in the neighbourhood — rooms are described consistently as spotlessly clean · the honest caveat from reviews is that some beds feel harder than expected, and the windowless Superior can feel cramped if you are staying more than one night.

Pool, spa, and facilities — this is what sets S.D. Avenue apart from cheaper guesthouses in the same area · the hotel has an outdoor swimming pool with sun loungers, a genuine bonus at this price tier in Pinklao · the spa and Thai massage service draw consistent praise in reviews, with guests saying the quality of the massage therapists is excellent value · the Duangtip Restaurant serves Thai and international food, and the hotel has free Wi-Fi, on-site parking, and meeting rooms · the honest word from real guests: there have been periods when the pool was closed for maintenance with no prior warning on the website or at check-in · if the pool is your main reason for choosing S.D. Avenue, call the hotel (+66 2813-3111) to confirm it is open before you arrive — not just check a review from three months ago.

Breakfast and food — reviews give a mixed picture on breakfast · on the positive side: there is a reasonable spread of Thai and international dishes, and staff serving food are attentive · the honest limitation: the selection is narrower than at larger full-service hotels, and a few reviews note that quality varies day to day · breakfast costs an additional ฿110–330 per person depending on the package · if you want a wider morning-meal choice, the Pinklao area has plenty of local coffee shops and breakfast spots within a short walk or drive, which is actually a nice reason to explore the neighbourhood.

Staff and service — this is S.D. Avenue's clearest strength in the real-review picture · a service score of 9.0 on Trip.com reflects that staff here are genuinely friendly, proactive, and attentive · multiple reviews mention the front-desk team and housekeeping making guests feel warmly welcomed · the honest note: some staff have limited English, so international travellers who need complex communication should use a translation app · there is also a small number of reviews mentioning a less-than-friendly reception experience on specific occasions, though this is clearly the minority compared with the overall pattern.
"The room was clean and comfortable, the staff were very helpful and friendly. The pool was a nice plus. Location near Central Pinklao mall was very convenient."

What real reviews say — praise and gripes — compiled from Trip.com, Booking.com, and TripAdvisor · Praised consistently: very clean rooms; friendly, helpful staff; good value for Pinklao; outdoor pool and quality massage-spa at an accessible price; convenient for reaching the Southern Bus Terminal by Grab; walking distance from Lotus's Pinklao and local food vendors · Watch-out points: mattresses in some rooms are harder than expected; Wi-Fi can be slow and unreliable; the pool has been found closed during some stays without advance notice; breakfast selection is limited; the windowless Superior room feels claustrophobic for some; no in-room kettle or complimentary tea-coffee; some staff have limited English; and a ฿500 deposit is collected at check-in · overall, for the price bracket, these are manageable trade-offs, especially for travellers who are using the hotel primarily as a functional overnight stop.

Price and value — the price range for typical travel periods: Superior (no window) from about ฿1,290/night, Premier Room from about ฿1,750, Deluxe Room (32 sqm, floors 11–12) from about ฿2,100, and the Grand Deluxe with breakfast from ฿2,900 · rates climb during high season and long weekends, sometimes reaching ฿1,800–2,500+ for the same room type · measured against other Pinklao and Thonburi-west hotels, S.D. Avenue earns its keep by offering a pool, spa-massage, and consistently clean rooms at a price where comparable establishments elsewhere offer only a basic room · the trade-off is that you are staying in a 1993-era building without the polish of a newer hotel, and 15 minutes by Grab from the terminal rather than on its doorstep.

honestSummary: S.D. Avenue Hotel Bangkok is solid value for travellers who need a Thonburi-side overnight before a long-distance bus from the Southern Bus Terminal — clean rooms, genuinely helpful staff, an outdoor pool and spa at ฿1,300+/night · the honest caveats: no hotel shuttle to the terminal (budget 15 minutes by Grab), and confirm the pool is open before you arrive.
honestChecks: If you need to walk to the Southern Bus Terminal — no hotel anywhere near here is walkable to Sai Tai Mai; the terminal is off the main road → budget a 15-minute Grab (around ฿80–120) and book it in advance for very early departures.
If the pool is your main reason for booking — real guests have found the pool closed for maintenance without any website notice → call the hotel the day before to confirm it is open.

If you need a firm mattress or stable Wi-Fi — some beds skew hard, and Wi-Fi reliability varies → request a Deluxe room on floors 11–12, which earns better reviews on both counts than the windowless Superior.

tips.title: Pre-book your Grab to the terminal
tips.body: There is no hotel shuttle to the Southern Bus Terminal. For very early bus departures (4–6 a.m.), book your Grab the night before — the app can be slow to find drivers at that hour.

tips.title: Call ahead to confirm the pool
tips.body: Real guests have arrived to find the pool closed for maintenance with no advance notice online. Call +66 2813-3111 to check pool status before check-in if it matters to you.

tips.title: Upgrade to Deluxe (floors 11–12) if your budget allows
tips.body: The Deluxe Room at ฿2,100 gets you 32 sqm, city views, a window, and far better reviews than the windowless Superior — worth the modest step up for a comfortable night before a long journey.

tips.title: Use Central Pinklao as your base
tips.body: The mall is minutes away — stock up on snacks, grab a meal, pick up travel supplies, or exchange currency before your bus. Local street food is also plentiful immediately around the hotel.

faq.q: How far is S.D. Avenue Hotel from Bangkok's Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai)?
faq.a: About 6 km — roughly 15 minutes by Grab or taxi along Borommaratchachonnani Road, the same arterial road that runs toward the terminal · the hotel has no shuttle service, so plan to book a Grab in advance, especially for buses departing at 4–6 a.m. · Grab fares from the hotel to the terminal are typically ฿80–120.

faq.q: What does S.D. Avenue Hotel Bangkok cost per night?
faq.a: The Superior Room (no window) starts at about ฿1,290/night · Premier Room from about ฿1,750 · Deluxe Room (32 sqm, floors 11–12) from about ฿2,100 · rates rise during high season and public holidays · compare across Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com before you book, as prices move with demand.

faq.q: Does S.D. Avenue Hotel Bangkok have a pool?
faq.a: Yes, there is an outdoor swimming pool — but real guest reviews note that the pool has been closed for maintenance during some stays without advance notice on the website · call the hotel (+66 2813-3111) to confirm the pool is open before you check in if it is an important factor in your choice.

faq.q: Is S.D. Avenue Hotel Bangkok a good choice for long-distance bus travellers?
faq.a: Yes, particularly for anyone departing south or west from the Southern Bus Terminal on routes to Hua Hin, Kanchanaburi, Krabi, or Phuket · the hotel is on Borommaratchachonnani Road — the same road as the terminal, so the Grab ride is direct and short · you also get a pool, spa-massage service, and a restaurant to help you unwind before the journey.

faq.q: Is S.D. Avenue Hotel close to shopping in Bangkok?
faq.a: Yes · Central Pinklao is just a few minutes by car, and Lotus's Pinklao is walkable · for Siam, Sukhumvit, or Ari, expect 30–45 minutes by car depending on traffic, or use a taxi to connect to a BTS-accessible area.
